expected_level_description: You can: - track, log and correct information to protect assets and components
You can: - identify process optimisation opportunities with guidance, and contribute to the implementation of proposed solutions
You can: - resolve user requests, maintaining a high level of customer service - deal with complex complaints - use empathy to understand and meet customer needs

You can: - produce relevant reports in an appropriate format and agreed timeframe - work with stakeholders to discuss any changes in the reporting processes - interpret a data set and communicate this to others
You can: - own an issue until a new owner has been found or the problem has been mitigated or resolved

You can: - investigate problems in systems, processes and services, with an understanding of the level of a problem, for example, strategic, tactical or operational - contribute to the implementation of remedies and preventative measures
You can: - take inputs and establish coherent frameworks that work
You can: - show you have a Level 3 service management framework qualification
You can: - show an awareness of the relevant subject matter and a high level understanding of what it involves

You can: - identify and engage with users or stakeholders to collate user needs evidence - understand and define research that fits user needs - use quantitative and qualitative data about users to turn user focus into outcomes

You can: - explain the clinical and care workflows your work supports - use common health care terms correctly with clinical and care colleagues - recognise when a change could affect patient care and raise it
You can: - apply data protection principles to your work - contribute to data protection impact assessments - handle information requests and records correctly
You can: - create, change, and remove user accounts and access rights - check access against role-based access rules
You can: - monitor alerts and triage them using runbooks - gather evidence and escalate events - tune simple detection rules under guidance
You can: - explain how health IT systems can harm patients, for example through wrong, missing, or delayed information - report a possible clinical safety issue through the right route
